ap_biology-m06.stem: A student hypothesizes that the offspring of a monohybrid cross will appear in a 3:1 ratio. The table gives the observed and expected numbers. Using the chi-square equation and the critical values on the formula sheet, which statement is correct?

stimulus.description: Offspring phenotypes observed in a genetic cross and the numbers expected from the hypothesized ratio

options.text: The chi-square value is 2.00, which is less than the critical value of 3.84 (df = 1, p = 0.05), so the null hypothesis is not rejected.
options.why: Sums the squared differences without dividing by the expected counts.

options.text: The chi-square value is 0.05, which is less than the critical value of 5.99 (df = 2, p = 0.05), so the null hypothesis is not rejected.
options.why: Uses the number of phenotype classes as the degrees of freedom instead of the number minus one.

options.text: The chi-square value is 0.05, which is less than the critical value of 3.84 (df = 1, p = 0.05), so the null hypothesis is not rejected.
options.why: Sum of (o - e)^2/e over the 2 classes is 0.05. With df = 2 - 1 = 1, the critical value at p = 0.05 is 3.84, and 0.05 is less than 3.84, so the null hypothesis (the observed ratio matches 3:1) is not rejected.

options.text: The chi-square value is 0.05, which is greater than the critical value of 3.84 (df = 1, p = 0.05), so the null hypothesis is rejected.
options.why: Computes the statistic correctly but draws the opposite conclusion from the comparison with the critical value.

options.text: Stabilizing selection, because individuals with intermediate values were favored.

options.text: No selection occurred, because the trait still varies after selection.
options.why: Selection can change the shape or position of the distribution while variation remains.

options.text: Disruptive selection, because both extreme values of the trait were favored.
options.why: The distribution now has two peaks at the extremes and fewer intermediates.

ap_biology-m20.stem: The table shows the mean catalase activity with the range of ±2SE for three treatments. Which statement about the difference between the 37 °C treatment and the 60 °C treatment is best supported by the data?

stimulus.description: Mean catalase activity (mL of oxygen per minute) ± 2SE for three treatments, n = 10 for each treatment

options.text: The difference may be due to chance, because the ±2SE ranges of the two treatments overlap.
options.why: The ranges are 14.10 to 15.90 and 13.98 to 17.62, which overlap, so a real difference is not supported.

options.text: The difference is real, because the means are different values.
options.why: Different means alone do not show a real difference; overlapping ranges may reflect chance.

options.text: The difference is real, because the standard errors are small.
options.why: Small standard errors do not show a difference when the ranges overlap.

options.text: The difference cannot be assessed, because the table gives only the means.
options.why: The ±2SE values allow the ranges to be compared.

ap_biology-m21.set_intro: A researcher measures the rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction at four pH values. Each value in the table is the mean of the trials, with ±2SE.

stimulus.description: Mean rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction (µmol of product per minute) ± 2SE at four pH values

items.stem: Which statement best describes the data in the table?

options.text: The rate increases at every pH as the pH increases.
options.why: The rate at pH 10 is lower than at pH 8.

options.text: The rate is lowest at pH 8, and it is higher at both lower and higher pH values.
options.why: The pattern is the reverse of the table.

options.text: The rate is the same at all four pH values.
options.why: The means differ among the pH values.

options.text: The rate is greatest at pH 8, and it is lower at both lower and higher pH values.
options.why: The means rise to 18.6 at pH 8 and fall on either side, so the rate peaks at that pH.

key_conditions.condition: every quantity or fact needed is given in the stem or the stimulus

must_include: mean rates at four pH values

misconceptions.description: The rate at pH 10 is lower than at pH 8.
The pattern is the reverse of the table.
The means differ among the pH values.

verification.independent_path: argmax of the table means vs the generating optimum

blueprint.judgment_demand: choose the governing biological relationship, then apply or interpret it

items.stem: What is the percent change in the mean rate from pH 6 to pH 8?

options.why: Reports the difference in rates rather than the percent change.
Reverses the starting and ending means.
Percent change = (new - old) / old x 100 = (18.6 - 14.6) / 14.6 x 100 = 27%.
Divides the change by the larger mean instead of the starting mean.

items.stem: Which statement about the rates at pH 4 and pH 10 is best supported by the ±2SE values in the table?

options.text: The difference between the rates at pH 4 and pH 10 is real, because the means are different values.
options.why: Different means alone do not show a real difference when the ranges overlap.

options.text: The rates at pH 4 and pH 10 are equal, because both are enzyme-catalyzed.
options.why: The means are not identical, although the ranges overlap.

options.text: The difference between the rates at pH 4 and pH 10 cannot be judged without more trials.
options.why: The data already include 2SE ranges that can be compared.

options.text: The difference between the rates at pH 4 and pH 10 may be due to chance, because the ±2SE ranges overlap.
options.why: The ranges 5.62–6.58 and 6.24–7.56 overlap.

items.stem: Based on the data and on the structure of enzymes, which prediction about the rate at pH 12 is best supported?

options.text: At pH 12 the enzyme would catalyze a different reaction, because the active site would be larger.
options.why: A change in pH does not turn the enzyme into a catalyst for a different reaction.

options.text: At pH 12 the rate would be lower than at the optimum, because extreme pH can change the enzyme's shape and the active site.
options.why: Extreme pH disrupts ionic and hydrogen bonds that hold the enzyme's shape, which reduces substrate binding.

options.text: At pH 12 the rate would be the same as at the optimum, because enzymes work at all pH values.
options.why: Enzymes have an optimum pH and lose activity far from it.

options.text: At pH 12 the rate would be higher than at the optimum, because the substrate is more concentrated.
options.why: Changing pH does not concentrate the substrate.
